- [#37, working-rules] New projects meant for the todo-watcher need a folder on disk (local_path, e.g. a git-inited dir under ~/mesa-projects/projects/experiments/); without one tasks sit in todo. Person expected this to be remembered (session 125, project 43).
- [#44, working-rules] Cross-project work (session 134): a task that changes code in another project goes in that project, with a block on the dependency in the originating project so it doesn't start until that's done.
- [#47, decisions] Moves things between machines by opening another machine's Naru web UI in the browser (machines may run different Naru versions), not by copying files; same for the library. Portability features should work through the web UI (session 137, task 1430).
- [#51, decisions] Phone notifications go through vox (Telegram bot @NaruAiBot, project 45, cloned to tools/vox; this Mac is its dev machine), not ntfy or APNs (session 146).
- [#52, working-rules] Folder trust (session 146): when a new or moved project folder hits Claude Code's 'workspace not trusted' spawn failure, just mark it trusted myself (hasTrustDialogAccepted in ~/.claude.json projects) and re-touch the task — never hand it back to him.
- [#63, working-rules] Live responsiveness (session 150): run any shell command that might take more than a few seconds in the background so I can still hear and answer him; never recursive-search a whole repo (Rust target dirs are huge) — use helios or name source dirs.
- [#71, working-rules] Portability (session 160): Naru features must not depend on third-party API keys (e.g. Jev); prefer local models. Claude Code is the one external dependency he accepts. Tasks 1652/1653/1642 updated to drop Jev.
- [#73, machines-and-devices] Audio testing (session 163): use the BlackHole 2ch virtual device for all sound testing for now — never the real speakers/mic.
- [#74, decisions] Short replies (session 170): he often answers live with just yes, no or a number, so any voice filtering must never drop short utterances; fail open (task 1701/1703).
- [#78, decisions] Model roles decided (session 175): Sonnet for the live voice, Haiku for inbox-triage/retro (both switched 2026-10-09, tasks 1719/1720 done), Opus supervisor + Opus read-only planner, Sonnet implementers, all medium effort (tasks 1715-1720, Claude Config).
- [#79, machines-and-devices] Windows test machine (session 178, task 1742): ssh -i ~/.ssh/naru_windows 'thepredator\simon@192.168.0.157', key auth works, Windows 10. Use for Windows compat tasks 1740/1741; hard rule: never break Mac builds.
- [#80, working-rules] Windows (session 179): goal is a Windows installer on GitHub releases, not users building from source (task 1756); Windows changes must never affect Mac/Unix quality, put that rule in every Windows task. Ambient/native-only UI hidden in plain browser (task 1748 done).
- [#85, decisions] Live voice stays Sonnet (session 181): Haiku vs Sonnet voice test (task 1770) tied on score, Sonnet better on multi-turn voice case (97 vs 84); he chose to keep Sonnet despite Haiku's far lower cost.
- [#89, working-rules] [session 184] SendMessage/ListAgents: address a session by its full listed name (e.g. 'naru: Theming: ...'), not the short bracket code; the short code fails as unreachable.
- [#90, decisions] Concurrency (session 186): todo-concurrency stays 1 by his choice. Supervisors spawn in the project dir with no worktree (bgIsolation none), so same-project parallel tasks would collide; raising it first needs supervisors to start in their own worktree. merge-to-main is already safe.

- [#77, added 2026-10-09, last used -] ~/.claude is deliberately not a git repo: the person syncs changes back into Naru, which keeps a history of every file (session 175). Don't suggest git-init.

content.content: PreToolUse:Bash hook error: Blocked a no-op command (`echo hi`), which does nothing but spend a turn. Polling cannot observe an agent message -- completions arrive as harness notifications, so a shell loop burns a full context re-read per turn and learns nothing. Instead: wait on a real condition with Monitor (ToolSearch 'select:Monitor'), check ListAgents, read the agent's own transcript under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/subagents/, or stop and report to the user. If you must poll external state the harness cannot notify you about, pace it -- one `sleep <seconds>; <check>` sized to how fast that state actually changes.
